media_work.title: The Farm: Angola, USA
media_work.focus_or_theme: Life and death inside Louisiana State Penitentiary (Angola), perspectives of inmates serving long sentences (including life).
media_work.summaryNotes: Awarded Grand Jury Prize at Sundance Film Festival.

media_item.focus_or_theme: Life and death inside Louisiana State Penitentiary (Angola), perspectives of inmates serving long sentences (including life).

research_notes_other.notes_from_film_list.txt: Follows stories of several inmates at Angola Prison, including some who maintain their innocence. Available via YouTube, Amazon, DVD.
research_notes_other.research_findings: This highly regarded documentary offers a powerful look inside Angola. While the theme of potential innocence exists (particularly with Vincent Simmons), the film is more broadly about the human experience within the prison, covering parole hearings, the prison hospice, the execution process, and daily life.

featured_individuals.note_on_wrongful_conviction_focus: The documentary provides intimate portraits of these men's lives in prison. While some, notably Vincent Simmons, maintained their innocence, the film's primary focus is not an investigative deep-dive into proving/disproving these claims but rather a portrayal of life under extreme sentences at Angola. Searches did not identify specific segments focusing solely on wrongful conviction evidence for featured inmates. Details below pertain to Simmons, who strongly proclaimed innocence.
featured_individuals.full_name: Film follows six inmates: George Crawford
featured_individuals.exoneration_or_release_year: N/A (Remains incarcerated as of recent reports)
contributing_factors_raw: Simmons alleged inadequate defense, racial bias, flawed identification procedures.
